provenance_note: The chick-production dataset was previously targeted for a different island-coherence validation, whose workflow failed before producing a frozen result. This contract is prospective for the specific within-island-season association between breeding-group size and chicks per pair.

source.title: Adelie penguin colony-specific chick production, 1991, present.

question: Within the same Palmer island and breeding season, do smaller Adelie breeding groups produce fewer chicks per breeding pair than expected under equal per-pair reproductive success?

biological_hypothesis.name: small-group reproductive disadvantage
biological_hypothesis.prediction: Larger contemporaneous colony codes have higher per-pair chick production than smaller colony codes within the same island-season.
biological_hypothesis.mechanistic_scope: A positive size-performance effect is consistent with an Allee-like social or predation-mediated disadvantage of small groups, but does not by itself identify the mechanism.

season_definition: For January chick censuses, season_start_year = calendar year(time) - 1.

row_eligibility.duplicate_rule: If multiple usable rows share island, colony_code and season_start_year, retain the row with the largest num_chicks; break ties by largest num_breeding_pairs, then lexicographically smallest census_time. This rule is frozen before duplicate values are inspected and follows the general census practice of using the maximum count when multiple counts exist.

risk_set.size_variation_required: non-zero SD in log1p breeding-pair count
risk_set.predictor: log1p breeding-pair count, z-standardized within island-season for reporting; the null uses the exact pair counts.

primary_null.name: equal per-pair reproductive success
primary_null.conditioning: Condition separately on each island-season total chick count and the observed breeding-pair counts of all eligible colony codes.
primary_null.allocation: Under the null, total chicks C_g are allocated multinomially among colonies with probabilities p_i = pairs_i / sum_j pairs_j.
primary_null.meaning: Expected chick production is exactly proportional to breeding-pair count, so group size can change sampling variance but not expected chicks per pair.

primary_statistic.per_group_score: U_g = sum_i chicks_i*x_i - C_g*sum_i p_i*x_i, where x_i is within-group z(log1p pairs).
primary_statistic.interpretation: Positive Z means chick production is shifted toward larger groups beyond proportional expectation.

inference.simulation: For every draw, independently simulate each eligible island-season from its frozen multinomial null and recompute the same global Z.
inference.p_value: one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

effect_size.model: Conditional multinomial log-linear size effect within island-season: probability proportional to pairs_i * exp(beta*x_i).
effect_size.report: beta and exp(beta), where exp(beta) is the multiplicative change in expected chicks per pair for a 1-SD larger log group size within an island-season.
effect_size.role: descriptive effect size; Monte Carlo score test is the primary inferential gate.

sensitivities.exclude_litchfield: Repeat primary test after removing Litchfield Island.
sensitivities.leave_one_island_out: Repeat after removing each island in turn.
sensitivities.dirichlet_multinomial_cv10: Replace fixed multinomial probabilities by a Dirichlet-multinomial with concentration A=100 around proportional probabilities before allocating chicks.
sensitivities.exclude_duplicate_keys: Repeat the primary analysis after dropping every colony-season key that had more than one usable source row, regardless of which row would be retained.

decision_rule.support: Primary observed Z > 0 and one-sided Monte Carlo p <= 0.05.
decision_rule.stronger_pattern: Primary support plus positive observed Z in all five leave-one-island-out analyses and under both pair-count thresholds.
decision_rule.mechanistic_language: Even if supported, describe the result as small-group reproductive disadvantage or an Allee-like pattern, not as proof of skua predation or social facilitation.

interpretation_boundaries: Do not use the failed extinction-order exchangeability test as independent evidence for an Allee effect; the size-conditioned thinning null already showed that extinction ordering is mechanically expected.
Do not claim that colony_code is a mapped physical patch.
Do not infer predator causality without an independent predation measure.
Do not switch from chicks per pair to another reproductive endpoint after seeing this result.
Report the proportional null and overdispersion sensitivities regardless of outcome.
Report the number and identity count of duplicate colony-season keys and the exclude-duplicate-keys sensitivity.
